scope: Proposed Gallatin implementation and operating procedures for the MPN deployment. Status and requirements are drawn from the current assessment; configuration, approvals and completion are not implied by a proposal.

groups.title: Storage, keystore and backup protection
groups.content:
## MPN storage protection solution

Treat the eleven rules as four shared changes: host/keystore encryption, application storage binding, cryptographic integrity, and encrypted backup/restore. All are proposed **Needs work** recommendations; none assert that an unconfigured deployment already passes. Gallatin owns the implementation. The remaining provider/classification choices determine which implementation to commit, not whether a solution exists.

1. **Keep PostgreSQL and SeaweedFS.** Choose the existing host provider's encrypted disk/volume class and name the MPN binding `mpn-encrypted`. Set PostgreSQL `persistence.storageClassName`; `persistence.storageClass` does not drive its template. Add an optional `storageClassName` to the SeaweedFS PVC template or deliberately configure the cluster default. Cover Core identity DB, control-plane/datastore, node OS and temporary/cache storage; PVC encryption alone leaves temporary files and Secrets exposed at a different layer. Use API-server `--encryption-provider-config` or the distribution's supported encryption feature for Kubernetes Secrets, with a nonidentity provider first. Keys are separate from application/data-reader credentials.
2. **Enable object encryption already in the delivered product.** SeaweedFS4.52 has `-filer.encryptVolumeData` and `-s3.encryptVolumeData`; its existing cipher implementation uses AES256-GCM and rejects failed authentication tags. Expose and enable those server arguments rather than implementing crypto in every API. Protect filer metadata/chunk keys on the encrypted volume and include them in protected recovery material. Rewriting existing objects is needed to migrate old unencrypted content; toggling new writes is not retroactive. The exact4.52 upstream source establishes algorithm/flags, not the validated module path in the delivered Chainguard image. Keep encrypted block/storage protection in an approved module as the primary boundary; enable object AEAD as additional protection and bind its provider/module evidence before crediting it for a FIPS-specific check.
3. **Handle integrity explicitly.** Plain disk encryption/AES-XTS gives confidentiality; PostgreSQL page checksums detect corruption but are not cryptographic authentication. Existing SeaweedFS AES-GCM authenticates object ciphertext, with metadata/keys protected separately. Define the PII/classification/security-label data set and select an approved storage provider or supported host authenticated-integrity implementation for that live database scope. Linux already provides dm-crypt plus dm-integrity authenticated modes; use such a mode only where the chosen distribution/module supports the required approved operation and operational profile. This is a storage configuration/migration choice, not a proposal to add custom crypto to every DB page. Retain existing DB writer/admin restrictions as separate authorization controls. Signed authenticated backup manifests protect offline copies; they do not substitute for live-volume integrity. Keep these rules Needs work until the chosen integrity setting or accepted data-scope/provider mapping is implemented.
4. **Encrypt before offline export.** Reuse the backup workstream to produce a consistent PostgreSQL backup/WAL set and SeaweedFS data+metadata set on encrypted scratch. Package them using an existing authenticated encryption format such as CMS AES256-GCM with a signed version/hash manifest, executed with a pinned approved provider/module. Copy only the encrypted authenticated archive to offline media. Keep decryption/recovery authority separately, including an offline-capable key recovery procedure. Validate the full envelope before publishing restored data from isolated encrypted scratch. A provider-encrypted cloud object downloads as plaintext; Azure KeyVault backup blobs also are not portable offline private-key escrow.

**Optional Azure realization, only if Azure/AKS is chosen:** use native Azure Disk CSI with `diskEncryptionSetID` where customer-managed keys are required, and choose node-pool `--enable-encryption-at-host` for host temporary/cache coverage. Native Azure managed disks have at-rest encryption already, so a new Rook/Ceph platform is unnecessary. A provider-neutral StorageClass binding still works for another MPN host. The existing app speaks S3; do not silently substitute a native Azure Blob endpoint as though protocols were interchangeable. Azure Blob can be an optional archive target with encryption and immutable completed backup objects, using a supported backup adapter. CMK/HSM is a requirement-dependent choice, not automatically required by every listed rule.

**Classification and module boundary:** this is a concrete baseline for stored-data confidentiality/integrity. Use the applicable validated cryptographic implementation for CUI/FIPS requirements. Classified MPN use requires its approved NSA/mission protection boundary; FIPS-capable disks or an AES algorithm name are not that approval. This dependency should remain visible in the mission-crypto decision, not leave all eleven technical solution rows unexplained.

**Acceptance from implementation artifacts:** committed host encryption settings; correct rendered PVC storage-class bindings; rendered SeaweedFS encryption flags; protected-key/recovery configuration with no real secrets committed; selected provider/host authenticated-integrity configuration; and backup/restore scripts that retain encryption outside the cloud. Negative fixtures should reject a modified encrypted object/archive and incorrect key. No live deployment, key creation, storage migration or backup export was performed.

groups.title: Certificate trust and deployment topology
groups.content:
## Gateway PKI and conditional topology solutions

These are proposed target settings and operating procedures. They are not deployed changes or new claims about the running MPN environment. Gallatin operates Core; the mission authority supplies only mission designation and approved issuance/CA decisions.

### Approved gateway certificates and restrictive verification

1. Gallatin SRE owns the gateway certificate lifecycle. Prepare a CSR using the actual MPN tenant/admin host SANs; prefer explicit SANs where mission issuance policy disallows wildcards. Route it through the mission-authorized DoW/CNSS NPE/server certificate issuance process or an explicitly approved external-PKI equivalent. A FIPS image does not select certificate assurance/class. A generic public certificate is not automatically approved or disapproved: record its issuer/policy approval.
2. Deliver full-chain `tls.crt`, private `tls.key`, and the approved client CA roots (`cacert`, when client-certificate verification is selected) through the protected secret process. Create separate Secrets in `istio-tenant-gateway` and `istio-admin-gateway`; do not commit keys to this tracker. Existing Core supports these references:

```yaml
## Core package bundle overrides; example names, not actual production secrets.
overrides:
  istio-tenant-gateway:
    uds-istio-config:
      values:
        - path: tls.credentialName
          value: mpn-tenant-gateway-tls
  istio-admin-gateway:
    uds-istio-config:
      values:
        - path: tls.credentialName
          value: mpn-admin-gateway-tls
```

Retain Core's HTTPS/TLS1.3 gateway. `OPTIONAL_MUTUAL` on the SSO host permits password+OTP alongside CAC; select `MUTUAL` only for a mission certificate-only path. Configure the client CA in the referenced secret for the selected mode. API containers remain protected by mesh plus the gateway; there is no need to reimplement public TLS per application container.

3. Publish an explicit approved-root bundle through Core. Start from `CA_BUNDLE_INCLUDE_DOD_CERTS: "true"`, `CA_BUNDLE_INCLUDE_PUBLIC_CERTS: "false"`; use `CA_BUNDLE_CERTS` only for named, approved additional chains. Do not turn on the whole public bundle to work around a missing service CA. Every exception is tied to a needed service and documented approved issuer. Confirm that the DoD external-PKI root set actually selected is appropriate for the mission's assurance policy.
4. Mount `uds-trust-bundle` at a read-only path in the API; for its Node HTTPS/JWKS verification use an explicit per-client `ca` configuration, or `--use-openssl-ca` with `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing to the curated PEM and `SSL_CERT_DIR` pointing to a controlled empty/curated directory. Preserve existing FIPS/startup options when adding Node options. Remove conflicting additive/system-root choices. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` alone only adds roots and does **not** enforce the rule's restrictive trust set. Scope CA restrictions to the actual protected-session verifier; local mesh workload certificates and externally approved server certificates have separate trust mappings. Apply equivalent per-client CA settings for other service runtimes that initiate relevant TLS.
5. Keep the certificate evidence record in the compliance package: host/SAN, issuer and approved assurance/class/certificate-policy OID, public-chain fingerprint, validity, renewal owner, approved CA set, and secret reference. Validate the public chain and exact hostname offline against approved roots; keep fixtures showing that an unrelated CA is rejected. Secret manager/certificate automation should rotate material before expiration and retain old/new public fingerprints, without exposing keys. This closes a specified provisioning/control task; evidence is not a request for a DU-managed-cluster attestation.

### HA design versus MAC I deployment

V-222595 asks about redundancy design, which the templates already support. V-204814 additionally requires an actual HA cluster **if** the mission declares MAC I. Mission authority records MAC I true/false; this policy choice cannot be invented from source.

For a required HA target, deploy Core/ingress and the application on at least three schedulable nodes across the available fault domains. Configure each stateless web/API service with at least two replicas (or HPA `minReplicas: 2`), readiness/liveness, PDB `minAvailable: 1`, and node/zone spreading. Example existing common-chart settings:

```yaml
replicaCount: 2
pdb:
  enabled: true
  minAvailable: 1
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: horizon-api
```

Use the matching release label for each service; add zone spread only when multiple zones actually exist. HPA CPU scaling also requires meaningful CPU requests. PDBs limit voluntary disruptions; they do not prevent hardware failure or make a singleton stateful service redundant.

Complete stateful dependencies explicitly: replace the selected single-node PostgreSQL topology with a supported HA PostgreSQL primary/standby setup and stable failover endpoint (or approved external HA PostgreSQL); do not merely set StatefulSet replicas greater than one on independent unreplicated PGDATA. Use a properly configured clustered NATS/JetStream deployment with replicated streams and separate durable volumes, redundant object storage/storage backend, and HA Core identity/database/gateway dependencies. Select storage/cluster products supported in the MPN environment, with an owned failover/restore procedure and approved recovery objectives. Multiple stateless replicas alone do not satisfy this whole-service requirement. If MAC I is false, retain the source-capability mapping and submit the exact rule's N/A.

### Conditional DoW DMZ tier isolation

The mission authority records whether the approved MPN network boundary is a DoW DMZ. Do not equate private DNS, `uds.dev`, classification discussion, or a namespace with that designation.

If the tiered app is in the DoW DMZ, Gallatin replaces broad `IntraNamespace` permissions with three default-deny tier namespaces/Packages: `horizon-web`, `horizon-app`, `horizon-data`. A diagram and policy matrix state the following target flows:

| Source | Destination | Allowed target |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant ingress gateway | Web | Static HTTP port3000 |
| Tenant ingress gateway | API | API port3001, declared API routes |
| Tenant ingress gateway | NATS websocket endpoint | Only selected websocket8443 route |
| API/authorized workers | PostgreSQL | TCP5432 with explicit destination namespace/pod selector |
| API/authorized workers | NATS | Declared service ports only |
| API/authorized workers | Object storage/model runtime | Approved local endpoints/ports only |
| Web pod | API/database | No direct pod-to-pod access; browser calls the public API route |
| Each selected tier | DNS, approved telemetry, identity | Explicit infrastructure/service peers and required ports only |

Each application pod remains mesh enrolled. Peer rules combine namespace and pod selectors in a **single** peer when both are needed, rather than accidentally OR-ing all namespaces/all pods. Remove the old broad permissions: Kubernetes policies are additive, so a narrow policy does not cancel an existing allow-all. Namespace separation requires updating chart namespaces, service FQDN references and Package exposures; the static browser's public API/SSO origin need not change merely because backend namespaces change. Keep administrative access on the separately controlled Core admin path. Have the mission accept this logical network segmentation against the actual DMZ boundary requirements; NSA/CISA guidance supports pod/namespace policy isolation as a Kubernetes segmentation mechanism. If not in the DoW DMZ, record the exact conditional N/A instead of implementing a fictitious DMZ deployment.

groups.title: Account, audit, access and training procedures
groups.content:
## Governance actions

Gallatin operates the Horizon/UDS deployment on MPN. These actions use the existing identity, logging, release and company-policy mechanisms. Prepared checklists are not claims that a review, training course or authorization has been completed.

| Rule | Suggested status | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| V-222412 | Needs work | Gallatin SRE exports the scoped UDS/Horizon human-account list to a controlled record; the mission account owner marks each retained/removed with a business justification and date, and the authorized operator carries out approved removals. | Gallatin SRE operator and MPN mission account owner |
| V-222433 | Needs work | Adopt the prepared identity-verification, authorized-unlock and audit-record procedure for Gallatin-operated UDS; obtain named MPN ISSO/ISSM acceptance and retain its version. | Gallatin UDS identity administrator; MPN ISSO and ISSM |
| V-222622 | Needs work | Gallatin SRE and the designated security reviewer perform the prepared Loki/Grafana event review, disposition exceptions, record its date and set the next review due under the quarterly policy. | Gallatin SRE; designated MPN ISSO/security reviewer |
| V-222628 | Needs work | Ian/Gallatin SRE derives the external-enclave flow rows from the selected MPN overlay and existing System Impact Assessment; the security lead routes them to the MPN network/PPSM authority for CAL compliance review and approval. | Gallatin SRE/Ian; security lead; MPN network/PPSM approving authority |
| V-222629 | Needs work | The Gallatin security lead and MPN sponsor submit the approved Horizon MPN flow set through the applicable PPSM/eMASS process and record the resulting identifier or written registration exemption in the controlled authorization packet. | Gallatin security lead and MPN Government sponsor/PPSM authority |
| V-222630 | Likely covered | Record the managed-service responsibility boundary and current GitHub assurance-report references; review the actual repository controls and obtain acceptance of any applicable provider-side STIG tailoring in the development authorization packet. | Gallatin GitHub organization owner and security/compliance lead |
| V-222631 | Needs work | The GitHub organization owner and Horizon engineering owner certify the protected Nov10 entitlement snapshot, justify each privileged role, record approved changes and review again within three months. | GitHub organization owner; Horizon engineering owner; security reviewer |
| V-222673 | Needs work | Program management and security training owners add the prepared role-specific secure-SDLC module to ThreatSwitch, assign all application roles, record completion/assessment and refresh annually. | Program manager; security training owner/FSO; engineering managers |

The read-only GitHub entitlement snapshot is prepared; no account changes were made. Human rosters, report bodies and sensitive event details belong in controlled evidence storage. Only record identifiers, dates, summary disposition and links belong in the public tracker.

### V-222412

The product uses UDS identity and individual accounts; no additional account-discovery implementation is needed. Complete the mission human-account certification against the current approved personnel list. Required service accounts are excluded by the official check. This is a defined account-owner review action rather than an unresolved runtime behavior.

Cadence: Before mission account enablement, on joiner/mover/leaver events, and quarterly under the existing access-review policy.

1. Export only identities entitled to the Horizon MPN tenant, including inherited groups and privileged roles.
2. Separate human identities from necessary service identities.
3. Match each human to the approved mission roster and role; record retain/modify/remove, owner reason, review date and ticket.
4. Have the mission account owner certify decisions; an authorized operator executes approved changes and records completion.

Complete when: All in-scope human accounts have an accountable owner and certification; approved unnecessary-account removals are recorded.

### V-222433

UDS Keycloak already provides account lockout and administrator recovery, and corporate policy requires identity verification. Complete the short operational unlock procedure and its explicit ISSO/ISSM approval; do not build a second unlock API.

Cadence: For every account-unlock event; reapprove on a material identity/recovery change.

1. Open an incident/help-desk request recording realm and account identifier without passwords or recovery secrets.
2. Verify requester identity using the approved independent channel or sponsor/CAC/PIV process; never rely solely on the locked account session.
3. Confirm employment/mission entitlement and investigate suspicious lockouts before recovery.
4. An authorized UDS identity administrator resets the brute-force lock using native Keycloak administration; require credential reset or session revocation when compromise is suspected.
5. Retain request, verification method, administrator, timestamp, reason and native administration-event reference; close the request.

Complete when: ISSO and ISSM accept the versioned procedure and the operator can produce a complete recovery record when an unlock occurs.

### V-222622

The review tooling and quarterly procedure exist. Establish and record the first scoped MPN audit review, then follow the same cadence and event-driven reviews. A Grafana dashboard is an enabling mechanism, not a dated security review.

Cadence: Quarterly under the existing policy and immediately upon identified security events, as the official check requires.

1. Define review window, deployed release and included audit sources; verify the required sources delivered records throughout the window.
2. Review denied authentication and authorization, account/role/realm changes, privileged actions, deployment/configuration changes, suspicious data access and audit interruption/tampering alerts.
3. For each exception, record query/time range, event references, triage, disposition and linked incident or remediation ticket.
4. Reviewer records date, conclusions, source omissions and next due date; retain a restricted review record with traceable evidence.

Complete when: A dated review is retained and no review interval exceeds the approved policy; security-event-triggered reviews have tickets.

### V-222628

Delivered configuration and existing System Impact Assessment identify the network flows. Complete the MPN-specific external-enclave ports/protocols classification and authority submission; reuse the flow inventory and default-deny policy rather than redesign networking or register every pod port as external.

Cadence: Before production authorization and before adding/changing an external-enclave service or port.

1. Use the current MPN architecture boundary and deployment configuration, not the separate DU or III Corps IATT inventory.
2. Separate browser/gateway, identity, permitted mission-data interfaces and required platform service flows from purely internal pod/service flows.
3. For each external flow, record direction, protocol/port, endpoints, service function, release/profile, encryption/authentication and the PPS CAL disposition.
4. Have the MPN network authority confirm the applicable boundary and accepted CAL entries; record approval or exact conditions.
5. Keep approved rows synchronized with the generated UDS Package/network policies on each affected release.

Complete when: External-enclave flows have an accepted MPN CAL mapping and approval record; configuration matches that mapping.

### V-222629

A source-controlled flow table cannot itself create the production registration required by this check. Complete a concrete MPN registration action using the same approved flow set; retain an authority-issued registration identifier or explicit exemption, without treating a draft from another program as completion.

Cadence: Before production authorization and when a registered service/port/release boundary materially changes.

1. Identify the MPN system/authorization record and responsible PPSM registration authority with the Government sponsor.
2. Submit the approved external-flow inventory from V-222628 using the required authority template.
3. Resolve required endpoint/system identifier fields and retain submission receipt and authority decision.
4. Record registration ID, date, scope/release and approved flows, or the authority-issued exemption and rationale.

Complete when: The production MPN authorization packet contains a valid registration or written authority determination that registration is not required.

### V-222630

Horizon uses provider-operated GitHub Enterprise Cloud, with enforced repository reviews, CodeQL and change controls. GitHub manages the hosting software; applying a customer Git-server/OS patch checklist to this SaaS instance would create a fictitious server obligation. Record scoped provider inheritance using GitHub assurance reports and retain Gallatin responsibility for organization/repository settings. SOC/ISO reports support that mapping but are not called a DISA STIG certificate.

Cadence: On adoption, material GitHub hosting/enterprise-policy change, and annual provider-assurance refresh as a proposed operating cadence.

1. Document provider-operated GitHub.com Enterprise Cloud as the CM service; distinguish it from self-hosted Enterprise Server.
2. Organization owner obtains current SOC2/ISO/CSA and relevant continuity/security reports through organization Settings → Security → Compliance.
3. Map provider hosting/patching duties to GitHub; map repository access, rulesets, review gates, security scanning, integrations and audit retention to Gallatin.
4. Retain report dates, boundary, repository settings snapshot and security acceptance of the tailored provider-side evidence; do not publish licensed reports.

Complete when: Provider inheritance and customer controls are recorded and accepted for the development boundary; no unsupported claim of a GitHub STIG certificate is made.

### V-222631

Use a read-only effective-entitlement snapshot of the Horizon repository for the quarterly access-certification workflow. Record accountable owner decisions against the full effective grant list.

Cadence: At least every three months; also on departures and material role changes.

1. Compare effective memberships, team/default grants, outside collaborators, invitations and installed automation permissions with active engineering responsibilities.
2. Each human role receives retain/change/remove with owner rationale; individually justify admin or bypass authority.
3. Review relevant GitHub membership/permission-change audit history since the preceding review.
4. Owner certifies the decisions and an authorized administrator executes approved changes separately; retain the completed record and next due date.

Complete when: Every current grant is certified and approved changes are complete, with a dated retained record no more than three months old.

### V-222673

The corporate annual training platform and general awareness courses exist. Assign and record role-appropriate secure-development instruction for every application manager, designer, developer and tester; general awareness or CAC/SIPR training alone does not meet this explicit SDLC requirement.

Cadence: At least annually for all relevant application roles; include new staff before independent security-sensitive duties and keep the existing hire-training deadline.

1. Map current personnel to one or more application roles without publishing the roster.
2. Assign the approved secure-SDLC course plus applicable role modules in ThreatSwitch.
3. Use attendance plus completion assessment or equivalent recorded demonstration; capture date and course/version.
4. Managers resolve missing completion and the program manager verifies full role coverage, then schedules annual refresh.

Complete when: All application roles have annual role-relevant secure-development completion records, distinct from generic security-awareness assignments.

groups.title: Mission classification and PII processing
groups.content:
## Classified encryption

MPN will process classified data. The classified-encryption rules apply.

For each relevant component, identify the encryption implementation protecting its data, check whether it meets the rule's NSA-approved requirement, and configure missing protection. Record the product/module, approval reference and required settings. Reuse approved encryption already supplied by the host, storage or network; no duplicate application crypto is required.

For PostgreSQL V-233495, read the discussion as well as the title: it addresses DBMS compatibility with NSA-approved encryption devices. Identify the MPN encryption protecting PostgreSQL and confirm the database paths use it. Credit that protection rather than requiring a separate NSA certificate for the PostgreSQL container. CMVP5132 establishes its software module validation; it does not by itself answer the infrastructure-coverage check. See [the requirement interpretation](../NSA-CRYPTOGRAPHY.md).

The ASD V-265634 check has a specific non-SAMI/SAMI distinction: it permits NIST-certified cryptography for stored non-SAMI data as required by the owner and requires NSA-validated Type1 for stored SAMI. Use that wording when checking the implementation; do not impose Type1 on every component merely because the environment is classified.

## Classification guide

Use the existing program/mission classification guide if it covers Horizon's data elements, as V-222664 permits. Record its identifier and applicable sections. Extend the guide only for uncovered data; the guide requirement is separate from checking whether a cryptographic implementation is approved.

## PII processing metadata

Approve the permitted processing and purposes for the actual PII fields. Reuse document `files.tags` and propagated metadata for `privacy.profile`, `privacy.authorized_processing`, `privacy.processing_purpose` and `privacy.policy_ref`. Add only the missing schema/API associations for account identity fields. Validate presence, allowed values, propagation and protection against unauthorized tag removal.

Use the mission-data protection record template for the field/purpose associations and the governing guide references. A proposed tag profile is not an implemented control or an approved guide.
